summary: The State of Punjab challenged the High Court's judgment directing it to issue a fresh notification providing 1% reservation for children/grandchildren of terrorist-affected and Sikh riot-affected persons in all private unaided non-minority Medical/Dental institutions, including management quota seats, and 3% sports quota in Government Medical/Dental Colleges. The State argued that the High Court erred in issuing a writ of mandamus compelling reservation policy, which is an executive prerogative under Article 15(5) of the Constitution. Reliance was placed on precedents holding that reservation policy decisions are within the State's discretion. The respondents argued the issue had become academic as a new notification for 2021-22 had already implemented similar reservations. The case involved questions on judicial overreach into policy matters and the extent of judicial review in reservation policies.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 15(5) of the Constitution of India
Gulshan Prakash (Dr.) and others v. State of Haryana and others, (2010) 1 SCC 477
Chairman and Managing Director, Central Bank of India and others v. Central Bank of India SC/ST Employees Welfare Association and others, (2015) 12 SCC 308
Suresh Chand Gautam v. State of Uttar Pradesh and others, (2016) 11 SCC 113
Mukesh Kumar and another v. State of Uttarakhand and others, (2020) 3 SCC 1
final_judgment: The appeals were disposed of keeping the question of law open, as the issues had become academic in light of the subsequent notification for the academic year 2021-22 that implemented the challenged reservations.
